chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, who said:

Ali ibn Bilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Sometimes a person dies with us and the ground is damp, so we spread the grave with saaj (wood) or we cover it. Is that permissible?' So he wrote: 'That is permissible.'

key_terms.السَّاجِ: Saj (a type of wood or timber used for flooring or covering)
key_terms.نَدِيَّةً: Damp or moist (referring to the soil)
key_terms.نُطْبِقُ: We cover or seal (referring to covering the grave)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use wood or cover a grave if the ground is damp?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of using wood (*saaj*) or covering the grave to protect the deceased from damp earth, a practical adaptation for burial conditions. It underscores the flexibility in grave construction (*lahad*) within Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the preservation of the body against moisture without altering the fundamental burial rites.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany who said,

‘Ali Bin Bilal wrote to Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes someone dies with us and the ground happens to be damp, so we pave the grave with the wood, or we re-inforce upon it. Is that Permissible?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘That is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasaniy who has said the following:

“Once Ali ibn Bilal wrote to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the condition of a grave asking, ‘Someone may die in our area but the ground of the grave is wet.’ We pave it (the floor) with teak (wooden board) or cover it in this way, is this permissible? He (the Imam) wrote the answer, ‘It is permissible.’” H 4536, Ch. 64, h 2
